lessons.name: aibo ERS-1000
lessons.summary: aibo ERS-1000 is Sony's 2018 robot dog, with 22 axes of movement, cameras and cloud services to behave like a companion pet.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

aibo ERS-1000 is Sony's 2018 robot dog, with 22 axes of movement, cameras and cloud services to behave like a companion pet.

![Photo of a Sony aibo ERS-1000 robot dog](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-aibo.webp)
*Photo of a Sony aibo ERS-1000 robot dog. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aibo_ERS-1000_-_1.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A pet robot is a shipped product:** Sony released it in Japan on 11 January 2018 at 198,000 yen, according to its 2017 announcement.
- **Part of the brain lives online:** the announcement says an **aibo Basic Plan** subscription is needed, so the robot depends on Sony's cloud.
- **Motion here means expression:** its axes move the head, mouth, ears and tail, not only the legs.

> **Key idea:** aibo's engineering goal is believable character, not speed or payload, so sensing people matters more than terrain.

Think of aibo like a mobile app with a backend. The robot is the client that senses and acts, while the subscription service runs on the server side.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Actuators** (motor units that turn commands into motion) are ultracompact 1-axis and 2-axis designs developed by Sony.
- **Two OLED eyes** display expressions; OLED is a thin, self-lit screen technology.
- **A 64-bit quad-core CPU** runs on board, with LTE and Wi-Fi for connectivity.
- **Sensors** include two cameras, a time-of-flight sensor, touch sensors, two 6-axis IMUs and four microphones.
- **One camera supports SLAM**, letting the robot build a map while locating itself.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Release (Japan)** | 11 January 2018 |
| **Actuated axes** | 22 |
| **Size** | approx. 180 × 293 × 305 mm |
| **Mass** | approx. 2.2 kg |
| **Power use** | approx. 14 W |
| **Battery / recharge** | approx. 2 h / approx. 3 h |

## Key terms

- **Axis**: one independently driven direction of motion, like one joint.
- **IMU**: inertial measurement unit; it senses rotation and acceleration.
- **Time-of-flight sensor**: measures distance by timing reflected light.
- **SLAM**: simultaneous localization and mapping.
- **OLED**: organic light-emitting diode display.

## Getting started

1. **Read Sony's 2017 announcement** and list which sensors serve people versus navigation.
2. **Open the official aibo site** and look for the developer and visual programming material it links.
3. **Read the AIBO history article** to see how the ERS-1000 relates to earlier models.
4. **Compare it with Petoi Bittle**, a small open quadruped you can program directly.

## Used in

- **Built by Sony:** the map links aibo ERS-1000 only to its maker, with no map project using it yet.
- **Best used as a reference:** compare its expressive design with research quadrupeds such as Unitree Go2 and Stanford Pupper.

lessons.name: ANYmal
lessons.summary: ANYmal is a dog-sized quadruped from ETH Zurich and ANYbotics, built with torque-controllable legs to walk, climb and inspect industrial sites autonomously.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ANYmal is a dog-sized quadruped from ETH Zurich and ANYbotics, built with torque-controllable legs to walk, climb and inspect industrial sites autonomously.

![Photo of an ANYmal robot inspecting a power substation](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-anymal.webp)
*Photo of an ANYmal robot inspecting a power substation. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anymal-robot-inspection-power-grid.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is a landmark for learned walking:** a 2019 Science Robotics paper trained a neural-network policy in simulation and ran it on ANYmal.
- **That policy followed velocity commands:** the authors report faster running and recovery from falls than earlier controllers.
- **It is also a real product:** ANYbotics sells ANYmal for autonomous inspection of industrial plants.

> **Key idea:** ANYmal shows the full path from research controller to deployed inspection robot.

A software analogy: the research version is the open-source prototype, and the inspection product is the hardened, supported release.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Compliant, precisely torque-controllable actuators** drive each leg; torque control means commanding force rather than only position.
- **Lasers and cameras** let it map its surroundings and localize itself, per ETH's Robotic Systems Lab.
- **A planner** chooses a path and footholds, so the robot picks where each foot lands.
- **The product version** carries visual, thermal and acoustic inspection sensors on a pan-tilt unit.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Mass (ETH RSL page)** | under 30 kg including payload |
| **Protection** | IP67 (product page) |
| **Walking speed** | 0.75 m/s |
| **Range** | 2 km |
| **Walking time per charge** | 90–120 min |
| **Extra payload** | 10 kg |

## Key terms

- **Torque control**: commanding how hard a joint pushes, which lets legs absorb impacts.
- **Policy**: a learned function that maps observations to actions.
- **Sim-to-real**: training in simulation, then running on hardware.
- **Foothold**: the planned contact point for a foot.
- **IP67**: a rating for dust-tight and water-immersion protection.

## Getting started

1. **Read the ETH RSL ANYmal page** to see the research goals in plain language.
2. **Skim the 2019 paper's abstract** and note what was trained in simulation.
3. **Study the product page specifications** and compare them with research needs.
4. **Watch an official video** and pause on stairs and recoveries.

## Used in

- **ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab (RSL)** builds and uses ANYmal in research.
- **Knowledge links:** RL locomotion with sim-to-real, and Fall recovery & get-up, both use ANYmal as a reference platform.
- **Related robot:** ANYmal X is the explosion-protected inspection variant.

lessons.name: ANYmal X
lessons.summary: ANYmal X is ANYbotics' explosion-protected quadruped for autonomous inspection inside hazardous industrial areas where flammable gas may be present.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ANYmal X is ANYbotics' explosion-protected quadruped for autonomous inspection inside hazardous industrial areas where flammable gas may be present.

![Photo of ANYmal X at an Equinor plant](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-anymal-x.webp)
*Photo of ANYmal X at an Equinor plant. Source: [ANYbotics](https://www.anybotics.com/robotics/anymal-x/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Certification shapes the whole design:** the official page lists **ATEX Zones 1 and 2**, the European rules for explosive atmospheres.
- **It shows what "industrial-grade" means:** sealing, flameproof parts and temperature monitoring matter as much as walking.
- **Customers exist:** a November 2026 news report says deliveries began, naming Equinor and DSM-Firmenich as first customers.

> **Key idea:** In hazardous sites, a robot must first be unable to ignite gas; inspection features come second.

A software analogy: certification is like a strict security audit, where the product cannot ship until every component passes.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Nitrogen-filled enclosures** keep explosive gas away from electronics, according to the news report.
- **Flameproof battery and leg actuators** are listed in the same report.
- **A protected sensor payload** carries a thermal camera, an acoustic imager and a zoom camera.
- **An optional gas module** adds gas sensing.
- **Docking** recharges the robot, and a **REST API** connects it to plant software.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Hazard certification** | ATEX Zones 1 and 2 |
| **Protection** | IP65 robot, IP67 payload |
| **Battery runtime** | more than 3 h |
| **Stairs** | up to 45° |
| **Thermal camera** | 640 × 512 |
| **Connectivity** | Wi-Fi 6, 5G/4G |

## Key terms

- **ATEX**: EU rules for equipment used in explosive atmospheres.
- **Zone 1 / Zone 2**: areas where explosive gas is likely or less likely.
- **Acoustic imager**: a sensor that locates sound sources, such as leaks.
- **Payload**: the equipment a robot carries.
- **REST API**: a web interface other software calls over HTTP.

## Getting started

1. **Read the official ANYmal X page** and sort features into safety, sensing and autonomy.
2. **Read the delivery news article** for the customer and certification context.
3. **Compare it with the original ANYmal** to see what explosion protection changes.
4. **Watch an official video** of an inspection round.

## Used in

- **Built by ANYbotics:** ANYmal X is the hazardous-area member of the ANYmal family.
- **Compare with DEEP Robotics Jueying X30**, another industrial inspection quadruped, to see what changes without hazardous-area certification.

lessons.name: Aru
lessons.summary: Aru is Nio Robotics' shape-changing inspection robot that switches between rover, snake, quadruped and tripod modes to reach confined industrial spaces.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Aru is Nio Robotics' shape-changing inspection robot that switches between rover, snake, quadruped and tripod modes to reach confined industrial spaces.

![Photo of Aru climbing stairs](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-aru.webp)
*Photo of Aru climbing stairs. Source: [Nio Robotics](https://nio-robotics.com/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **One body, four behaviours:** the official site describes **polymorphic** robots, meaning one machine that changes form for each task.
- **It targets real dirty jobs:** listed sites include hydro penstocks, ship hulls and heavy industry.
- **It is a French company:** the site says it is designed and assembled in Toulouse.

> **Key idea:** Aru trades a single specialised shape for a reconfigurable body, so mobility and tooling change per mission.

A software analogy: Aru works like one program with several run modes, each enabling different features for a different input.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Rover mode** uses **magnetic feet** to climb vertical steel surfaces.
- **Snake mode** passes hatches larger than 450 mm, 40 cm pipes and 90° bends.
- **Quadruped mode** handles stairs, ladders and uneven ground.
- **Tripod mode** stands steady to hold a tool, with a 15 kg reach listed.
- **Modular payloads** include laser decoating, airless painting, non-destructive testing probes and vision, with welding in development.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Maker** | Nio Robotics, Toulouse |
| **Modes** | Rover, Snake, Quadruped, Tripod |
| **Hatch access** | above 450 mm |
| **Pipe access** | 40 cm pipes, 90° bends |
| **Tripod tool load** | 15 kg (listed for tool reach) |
| **Mass and speed** | unknown |

## Key terms

- **Polymorphic robot**: a robot that changes its body shape for different tasks.
- **Magnetic adhesion**: holding onto steel with magnets instead of gravity.
- **Non-destructive testing (NDT)**: inspecting material without damaging it.
- **Decoating**: removing paint or coatings from a surface.
- **Penstock**: a large pipe that carries water to a hydroelectric turbine.

## Getting started

1. **Read the Nio Robotics site** and list which mode solves which obstacle.
2. **Watch a video of Aru** and note how it transitions between modes.
3. **Compare it with ANYmal X**, which keeps one shape and adds certification instead.
4. **Sketch one inspection mission** as a sequence of modes and tools.

## Used in

- **Built by Nio Robotics:** the map links Aru only to its maker, with no map project using it yet.
- **Ecosystem value:** a Toulouse robotics company is a possible French contact for industrial inspection topics.

lessons.name: Boston Dynamics Spot
lessons.summary: Boston Dynamics Spot is a 12-joint commercial quadruped whose public Python SDK lets developers command motion, read sensors and integrate custom payloads.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Boston Dynamics Spot is a 12-joint commercial quadruped whose public Python SDK lets developers command motion, read sensors and integrate custom payloads.

![Photo of two Spot robots carrying research payloads](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-spot-sdk.webp)
*Photo of two Spot robots carrying research payloads. Source: [Boston Dynamics](https://bostondynamics.com/products/spot/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Software students can start from code:** the official **Spot SDK** is a Python client library installed with pip.
- **It exposes real robot data:** examples read robot state, camera images, world objects and faults.
- **It teaches integration:** payload documents cover mechanical, electrical and software interfaces together.

> **Key idea:** On Spot, you rarely control motors directly; you send high-level commands to services and the robot handles balance.

A software analogy: the SDK is like a cloud provider's client library, where you call services instead of touching servers.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Two actuators in each hip (HX, HY) and one in each knee** give 12 degrees of freedom, three per leg.
- **Five pairs of stereo cameras** provide black-and-white images for perception.
- **The robot runs services**, such as state, image and E-Stop, which the SDK calls over the network.
- **A protocol definition** lets other languages talk to the same services.
- **Two payload ports** power and connect added hardware.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 12 |
| **Net weight** | 32.5 kg |
| **Maximum speed** | 1.6 m/s |
| **Typical runtime** | 90 minutes |
| **Max payload** | 14 kg |
| **SDK version (docs)** | 5.2.0 |

## Key terms

- **SDK**: software development kit, the libraries and examples for a platform.
- **Service**: a robot-side program answering requests, such as image capture.
- **E-Stop**: an emergency stop that cuts motion safely.
- **Degree of freedom**: one independent joint motion.
- **Payload interface**: the mounting, power and data connection for added hardware.

## Getting started

1. **Create a Python virtual environment**, as the quickstart recommends.
2. **Install the client packages** with `python3 -m pip install --upgrade bosdyn-client bosdyn-mission bosdyn-choreography-client bosdyn-orbit`.
3. **Read the hello_spot example** and identify authentication, lease and E-Stop steps.
4. **Study "About Spot"** for joint limits and specifications before planning motions.

## Used in

- **Knowledge links:** Perceptive rough-terrain locomotion and Loco-manipulation coordination use Spot as a reference robot.
- **Related node:** Spot (Boston Dynamics) covers the same robot as an inspection product.

lessons.name: DEEP Robotics Jueying Lite3
lessons.summary: DEEP Robotics Jueying Lite3 is a compact, roughly 12 kg quadruped sold for education, research and entertainment, with SDK APIs and payload modules.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

DEEP Robotics Jueying Lite3 is a compact, roughly 12 kg quadruped sold for education, research and entertainment, with SDK APIs and payload modules.

![Photo of Jueying Lite3 with people outdoors](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-lite3.webp)
*Photo of Jueying Lite3 with people outdoors. Source: [DEEP Robotics](https://www.deeprobotics.cn/en/products/detail/7.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is sized for labs:** about 12 kg with battery, it is closer to a student platform than an industrial robot.
- **It is designed to be extended:** the official page lists **SDK APIs** and modular payloads for perception development.
- **Editions differ:** Trial, Discovery, Pro and Laser editions change sensors and features, so check before buying.

> **Key idea:** Lite3 is a teaching and research quadruped first; its value is open interfaces, not industrial ratings.

A software analogy: the editions work like software tiers, where higher plans unlock features such as LiDAR navigation.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **An octa-core 64-bit industrial processor** runs the onboard software.
- **A wide-angle camera, depth camera and ultrasonic sensors** support obstacle detection, depending on edition.
- **A microphone array and speaker** enable voice-command interaction.
- **Software features** include target following, front and rear obstacle stop, and autonomous navigation on higher editions.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Standing size** | approx. 610 × 370 × 406 mm |
| **Weight with battery** | approx. 12 kg |
| **Continuous payload** | 5 kg |
| **Unloaded runtime** | approx. 1.5–2 h |
| **Max operating speed** | 2.5 m/s |
| **Max stair height** | 15 cm |
| **Max slope** | 40° |

## Key terms

- **Edition**: a hardware and software configuration of the same robot.
- **Depth camera**: a camera that measures distance for each pixel.
- **Ultrasonic sensor**: measures distance with sound echoes.
- **Target following**: tracking and following a chosen person.
- **SDK API**: functions your code calls to command the robot.

## Getting started

1. **Read the official Lite3 page** and compare the edition columns.
2. **Browse the DEEP Robotics GitHub organisation** for published code.
3. **Watch an official video** of Lite3 moving.
4. **Compare it with Unitree Go2**, a similar-sized research quadruped.

## Used in

- **Built by DEEP Robotics:** the map links Jueying Lite3 only to its maker, with no map project using it yet.
- **Related node:** DEEP Robotics Jueying X30 is the company's larger industrial quadruped.

lessons.name: DEEP Robotics Jueying X30
lessons.summary: DEEP Robotics Jueying X30 is a 56 kg industrial quadruped for autonomous inspection, with IP67 protection, autonomous charging and low-light perception.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

DEEP Robotics Jueying X30 is a 56 kg industrial quadruped for autonomous inspection, with IP67 protection, autonomous charging and low-light perception.

![Photo of the Jueying X30 crossing obstacles](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-x30.webp)
*Photo of the Jueying X30 crossing obstacles. Source: [DEEP Robotics](https://www.deeprobotics.cn/en/products/detail/6.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It represents China's industrial legged robots:** DEEP Robotics markets X30 for inspection in harsh sites.
- **Its spec sheet shows real trade-offs:** tested top speed is **4.5 m/s**, while operating speed is **2.5 m/s**.
- **Payload changes runtime:** about 4 hours unloaded drops to about 2.5 hours loaded.

> **Key idea:** Industrial quadrupeds are judged on endurance, sealing and autonomy, not just headline speed.

A software analogy: the gap between tested and operating speed is like peak versus sustained throughput in a benchmark.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A sealed body** is rated IP67 and works from −20 °C to 55 °C.
- **Two octa-core processors** run perception and planning, with three on the Pro version.
- **Low-light perception** and obstacle avoidance support night inspection.
- **Autonomous charging, quick battery swap and an emergency stop** support long deployments.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Size** | 1000 × 470 × 695 mm |
| **Mass** | 56 kg (Pro 59 kg) |
| **Payload** | 20 kg |
| **Runtime** | approx. 4 h unloaded, 2.5 h loaded |
| **Speed** | 4.5 m/s tested, 2.5 m/s operating |
| **Stairs / slope** | 20 cm step, 30° slope |
| **Protection** | IP67 |

## Key terms

- **Inspection robot**: a robot that collects readings on a repeated route.
- **Autonomous charging**: docking to recharge without a human.
- **IP67**: dust-tight and protected against temporary immersion.
- **Operating speed**: the speed used in normal work, below the tested maximum.
- **Payload**: the extra equipment the robot carries.

## Getting started

1. **Read the official X30 page** and note which specifications are tested maximums.
2. **Watch an official video** of an inspection deployment.
3. **Compare it with ANYmal and Spot (Boston Dynamics)** on mass, payload and runtime.
4. **List the sensors** a plant inspection mission would need.

## Used in

- **Built by DEEP Robotics:** the map links Jueying X30 only to its maker, with no map project using it yet.
- **Related node:** DEEP Robotics Jueying Lite3 is the smaller education model.

lessons.name: KAIST HOUND 1
lessons.summary: KAIST HOUND 1 is a 45 kg research quadruped from KAIST's DRCD Lab, designed for fast, efficient running with an optimised gear train.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

KAIST HOUND 1 is a 45 kg research quadruped from KAIST's DRCD Lab, designed for fast, efficient running with an optimised gear train.

![Photo of HOUND 1 running on an athletics track](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-hound-1.webp)
*Photo of HOUND 1 running on an athletics track. Source: [KAIST](https://news.kaist.ac.kr/news/html/news/?mode=V&mng_no=33690), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It holds a speed record claim:** KAIST says HOUND ran 100 m in **19.87 s** from standing in October 2023, recognised by Guinness.
- **The run used one learned controller:** the lab credits a single **reinforcement learning** controller.
- **Design is treated as optimisation:** the ICRA 2022 paper picks gear ratios and gear geometry with mixed-integer nonlinear optimisation.

> **Key idea:** HOUND shows that fast legged running needs both a learned controller and hardware chosen by optimisation.

A software analogy: optimising the gear train is like tuning compiler flags against a benchmark before shipping.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Gear reductions** trade motor speed for torque; HOUND uses 4 at the hip and 119/15 at the knee.
- **The optimisation** considered gear ratio, gear geometry and motor heating limits together.
- **Long legs**, with 0.33 m thighs and 0.35 m calves, give long strides.
- **The lab publishes a URDF**, a robot description file usable in simulators.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Mass** | 45 kg |
| **Body size** | 0.7 × 0.2 × 0.14 m |
| **Thigh / calf** | 0.33 m / 0.35 m |
| **Max joint torque** | 50 Nm |
| **Slopes** | 22° |
| **Continuous walk** | 3.2 km |
| **Obstacles** | 35 cm |

## Key terms

- **Gear reduction**: a ratio that slows motor output and multiplies torque.
- **Torque**: rotational force, measured in newton-metres (Nm).
- **Reinforcement learning (RL)**: learning actions by trial and reward.
- **URDF**: Unified Robot Description Format, an XML file describing links and joints.
- **Mixed-integer optimisation**: searching over both discrete and continuous design choices.

## Getting started

1. **Read the KAIST HOUND 1 page** and compare its table with ANYmal's.
2. **Download the URDF** from the lab page and open it in a simulator such as MuJoCo.
3. **Read the ICRA 2022 abstract** to see which variables were optimised.
4. **Watch the record run video** and estimate stride length.

## Used in

- **Built and used by KAIST:** the map links HOUND 1 to KAIST as builder and user.
- **Related node:** KAIST HOUND 2 is the faster successor with in-house motors.

lessons.name: KAIST HOUND 2
lessons.summary: KAIST HOUND 2 is the successor to HOUND 1, a roughly 52–53 kg research quadruped with KAIST-built motors, drivers, gears and communications.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

KAIST HOUND 2 is the successor to HOUND 1, a roughly 52–53 kg research quadruped with KAIST-built motors, drivers, gears and communications.

![Photo of the KAIST HOUND 2 quadruped](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-hound-2.webp)
*Photo of the KAIST HOUND 2 quadruped. Source: [KAIST DRCD Lab](https://dynamicrobot.kaist.ac.kr/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **The lab moved to in-house hardware:** KAIST says HOUND 2 uses its own motors, drivers, gears and communication system.
- **It is described as faster than HOUND 1** and "faster than a human", but no exact speed is published on the page.
- **Numbers need care:** the page says 53 kg in text but **52 kg** in its table.

> **Key idea:** Owning the motor and driver stack lets a lab tune hardware for one goal, here running speed.

A software analogy: replacing bought motors with custom ones is like dropping a framework to write a faster, specialised runtime.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Custom motors and drivers** convert electrical commands into joint torque.
- **A reduction of 6** links the motors to the joints, according to the specification table.
- **Different torque limits** apply at hip and knee: 35 Nm and 30 Nm.
- **A URDF model** is offered for simulation, as for HOUND 1.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Mass** | 52 kg (table) / 53 kg (text) |
| **Thigh / calf** | 0.35 m / 0.33 m |
| **Torque constant** | 0.5881 |
| **Max torque hip / knee** | 35 Nm / 30 Nm |
| **Gear reduction** | 6 |
| **Top speed** | unknown |

## Key terms

- **Motor driver**: electronics that turn commands into motor current.
- **Torque constant**: torque produced per unit of motor current.
- **Gear reduction**: ratio trading speed for torque.
- **URDF**: a file describing a robot's links and joints for simulators.
- **In-house**: designed and built by the lab itself.

## Getting started

1. **Read the KAIST HOUND 2 page** and list what changed from HOUND 1.
2. **Compare both tables** and explain why lower gear reduction suits speed.
3. **Download the URDF** and load it in MuJoCo.
4. **Watch the HOUND 1 record-run video** as a baseline for judging later speed claims.

## Used in

- **Built and used by KAIST:** the map links HOUND 2 to KAIST as builder and user.
- **Related node:** KAIST HOUND 1 documents the record-setting predecessor and its optimised gear train.

lessons.name: Petoi Bittle
lessons.summary: Petoi Bittle is a palm-sized, servo-driven robot dog built around an Arduino-compatible board, designed for programming gaits and behaviours at low cost.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Petoi Bittle is a palm-sized, servo-driven robot dog built around an Arduino-compatible board, designed for programming gaits and behaviours at low cost.

![Photo of Petoi Bittle balanced on fingers](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-bittle.webp)
*Photo of Petoi Bittle balanced on fingers. Source: [Petoi](https://www.petoi.com/pages/bittle-open-source-bionic-robot-dog), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A desk-sized robot is a gentle start:** a palm-sized servo quadruped carries little risk on a desk.
- **The code is open:** Petoi's **OpenCat** framework is MIT-licensed on GitHub.
- **A map project targets Bittle:** Transfer a conservative gait to Bittle targets this robot.

> **Key idea:** Bittle swaps powerful motors for hobby servos, so you learn gait timing without industrial-robot risk.

A software analogy: a gait is like a loop of keyframes in an animation, replayed each cycle with small corrections.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Servos** are small motors that hold a commanded angle; each leg joint uses one.
- **The NyBoard V1** uses an Arduino Uno chip and carries an IMU and infrared receiver.
- **OpenCat** coordinates gaits, controls servos and integrates IMU data.
- **Interfaces** include serial, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi dongles, plus a Raspberry Pi option.
- **Newer Bittle X** uses an ESP32 board; OpenCat for older NyBoard is marked legacy.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Actuators** | servos |
| **Main board** | NyBoard V1 (Arduino Uno chip) |
| **Battery** | Li-ion, about 1 h walking |
| **Sensors** | IMU, infrared receiver |
| **Software** | OpenCat (MIT) |
| **Mass** | unknown |

## Key terms

- **Servo**: a motor with built-in position control.
- **Gait**: the repeating pattern of leg movements.
- **IMU**: senses tilt and rotation for balance.
- **Calibration**: setting each joint's zero position.
- **Arduino**: a family of microcontroller boards programmed in C++.

## Getting started

1. **Read the Petoi docs** for assembly and joint calibration.
2. **Calibrate every joint** before running any gait.
3. **Try the Skill Composer** to create a new pose sequence.
4. **Clone OpenCat** and read how gaits are stored.
5. **Send serial commands** from Python using the documented protocol.

## Used in

- **Map project:** Transfer a conservative gait to Bittle.
- **Knowledge links:** Gaits & gait cycles and Central pattern generators.
- **Related robot:** Stanford Pupper is a larger open quadruped used in the same project.

lessons.name: Pleurobot
lessons.summary: Pleurobot is EPFL BioRob's salamander-like robot with 27 degrees of freedom, designed from X-ray videos of real salamanders to walk and swim.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Pleurobot is EPFL BioRob's salamander-like robot with 27 degrees of freedom, designed from X-ray videos of real salamanders to walk and swim.

![Photo of the articulated Pleurobot](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-pleurobot.webp)
*Photo of the articulated Pleurobot. Source: [BioRob, EPFL; photo credit Konstantinos Karakasiliotis & Robin Thandiackal (2013)](https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/amphibious/pleurobot/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is biology turned into engineering:** researchers filmed a salamander with **cineradiography**, meaning X-ray video, tracking up to 64 skeleton points.
- **Design came from optimisation:** they chose which joints needed motors and which could stay passive.
- **It is a scientific instrument:** its main goal is to understand how the nervous system coordinates movement in vertebrates.

> **Key idea:** Pleurobot is built to copy an animal precisely, so the robot can test biological theories.

A software analogy: it is like a reference implementation built to match a specification exactly, so you can test the specification.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **27 actuated degrees of freedom** run along the body and segmented legs.
- **A low centre of mass** keeps it stable while walking.
- **A waterproof skin** lets it swim as well as walk.
- **Central pattern generators** (neural-like oscillators producing rhythms) are a core BioRob control approach.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Lab** | EPFL Biorobotics Laboratory (BioRob) |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 27 |
| **Model animal** | Pleurodeles waltl (salamander) |
| **Motion source** | X-ray video, up to 64 tracked points |
| **Modes** | walking, swimming |
| **Key paper** | J. R. Soc. Interface, 2016 |

## Key terms

- **Cineradiography**: X-ray filming of moving animals.
- **Degree of freedom**: one independently controlled joint motion.
- **Passive joint**: a joint without a motor that moves under forces.
- **Central pattern generator (CPG)**: a circuit that produces rhythmic signals without sensor input.
- **Biorobotics**: using robots to study and imitate animals.

## Getting started

1. **Read the Pleurobot page** and note the design steps.
2. **Read the 2016 paper abstract**, "From cineradiography to biorobots".
3. **Watch Auke Ijspeert's TED talk** on salamander robots.
4. **Compare it with Salamandra robotica**, an earlier, simpler amphibious robot.

## Used in

- **Built by EPFL Biorobotics Laboratory (BioRob):** the map links Pleurobot only to its maker.
- **Related knowledge:** Central pattern generators explains its rhythmic control approach.
- **Listed applications:** the lab mentions search-and-rescue and paleontology.

lessons.name: Salamandra robotica
lessons.summary: Salamandra robotica is EPFL BioRob's amphibious salamander robot that swims, crawls and walks using a spinal-cord-inspired central pattern generator controller.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Salamandra robotica is EPFL BioRob's amphibious salamander robot that swims, crawls and walks using a spinal-cord-inspired central pattern generator controller.

![Photo of Salamandra robotica II by a lake](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-salamandra.webp)
*Photo of Salamandra robotica II by a lake. Source: [EPFL; Kostas Karakasiliotis, Biorobotics Laboratory, EPFL](https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/amphibious/salamandra/), Free to use without prior permission with credit: Kostas Karakasiliotis, Biorobotics Laboratory, EPFL.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is a classic of bio-inspired control:** EPFL calls it the first robot combining swimming, serpentine crawling and walking.
- **One signal switches gaits:** the 2007 work shows that varying one stimulation level switches between swimming and walking.
- **Version II improved speed:** EPFL says Salamandra robotica II swims more than twice as fast as its predecessor.

> **Key idea:** A central pattern generator turns one simple "drive" value into a full, coordinated rhythm for every module.

A software analogy: a CPG is like a set of coupled timers, where one config value changes the whole schedule's tempo and pattern.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **The body is a chain of modules**, each with its own microcontroller, battery and motors.
- **Coupled nonlinear oscillators**, mathematical rhythm generators, run on the microcontrollers to model the spinal cord.
- **A laptop sends drive signals wirelessly**, and the oscillators produce the travelling body wave.
- **Version II adds foldable limbs**, so legs tuck in while swimming.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Lab** | EPFL Biorobotics Laboratory (BioRob) |
| **Modes** | swimming, crawling, walking |
| **Controller** | central pattern generator (coupled oscillators) |
| **Module electronics** | microcontroller, battery and motors per module |
| **Key papers** | Science 2007; IEEE T-RO 2013 |
| **Mass and size** | unknown |

## Key terms

- **Amphibious robot**: a robot working both on land and in water.
- **Central pattern generator (CPG)**: a neural-like circuit producing rhythmic output.
- **Oscillator**: a system that repeats a cycle, like a sine wave generator.
- **Drive signal**: a single input level that sets speed and gait.
- **Gait transition**: switching from one movement pattern to another.

## Getting started

1. **Read the EPFL Salamandra robotica page** for the robot's history.
2. **Read the 2007 Science abstract**, "From Swimming to Walking with a Salamander Robot Driven by a Spinal Cord Model".
3. **Simulate a chain of coupled sine oscillators** in Python and vary one drive value.
4. **Watch a swimming-to-walking video** and spot the gait change.

## Used in

- **Built by EPFL Biorobotics Laboratory (BioRob):** the map links Salamandra robotica only to its maker.
- **Related knowledge:** Central pattern generators uses the same control idea.
- **Related robot:** Pleurobot is BioRob's later, more anatomically detailed salamander robot.

lessons.name: Solo (ODRI open quadruped)
lessons.summary: Solo is the Open Dynamic Robot Initiative's open-source, torque-controlled quadruped built from low-cost brushless actuator modules and mostly 3D-printed parts.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Solo is the Open Dynamic Robot Initiative's open-source, torque-controlled quadruped built from low-cost brushless actuator modules and mostly 3D-printed parts.

![Photo of the Solo quadruped on a tabletop](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-solo.webp)
*Photo of the Solo quadruped on a tabletop. Source: [Open Dynamic Robot Initiative](https://open-dynamic-robot-initiative.github.io/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Everything is published:** hardware and software are released under the **BSD 3-Clause** licence.
- **It is buildable by a lab:** parts are mostly 3D-printed or off the shelf, per the ODRI site.
- **It is backed by research labs:** partners include MPI-IS, NYU Machines in Motion and LAAS-CNRS in Toulouse.

> **Key idea:** Solo makes torque-controlled legged robots reproducible by open-sourcing the actuator, not just the robot.

A software analogy: the actuator module is like a reusable library; Solo, Bolt and TriFinger are apps built on it.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Brushless actuator modules** combine a brushless motor, gearing and an encoder in one reusable unit.
- **Torque control** lets software command force directly, so legs can be compliant.
- **The BLMC µDriver and Master Board** handle motor control and communication.
- **Variants** include Solo8 with 8 joints and Solo12 with 12 joints.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Project** | Open Dynamic Robot Initiative (ODRI) |
| **Licence** | BSD 3-Clause |
| **Variants** | Solo8 (8 DoF), Solo12 (12 DoF) |
| **Actuator** | brushless actuator module |
| **Electronics** | BLMC µDriver, Master Board |
| **Key paper** | Grimminger et al. 2020 (arXiv 1910.00093) |

## Key terms

- **Brushless motor**: an efficient electric motor switched electronically.
- **Encoder**: a sensor measuring the motor's angle.
- **Torque-controlled robot**: a robot whose joints are commanded in force.
- **Open hardware**: designs published so others can build them.
- **Degree of freedom (DoF)**: one independent joint motion.

## Getting started

1. **Read the ODRI website** and the list of robots built on the module.
2. **Open the actuator hardware repository** and follow the step-by-step actuator assembly.
3. **Read the paper abstract** to see why the actuator design matters.
4. **Join the ODRI forum** before ordering parts.

## Used in

- **Open research platform:** the map has no builder or project edges for Solo yet.
- **Related knowledge:** Leg design & proprioceptive actuation covers the actuator ideas Solo uses.
- **French link:** LAAS-CNRS (Toulouse) is an ODRI partner.

lessons.name: Spot (Boston Dynamics)
lessons.summary: Spot (Boston Dynamics) is a commercial four-legged mobile robot for site inspection, carrying sensors over stairs and rough ground where wheels struggle.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Spot (Boston Dynamics) is a commercial four-legged mobile robot for site inspection, carrying sensors over stairs and rough ground where wheels struggle.

![Photo of Spot at an open-air motor show in Milan](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-spot.webp)
*Photo of Spot at an open-air motor show in Milan. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boston_Dynamics_Spot_in_Milan.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is the best-known commercial legged robot:** Boston Dynamics made Spot its first commercially available robot in 2019.
- **It went on public sale on 16 June 2020** at US$74,500, according to Wikipedia's Boston Dynamics article.
- **Industry buys it for data collection:** the product page focuses on inspection, autonomy and payloads.

> **Key idea:** Spot is sold as a mobile sensor platform; the value is the data it gathers on repeatable routes.

A software analogy: Spot is like a scheduled job runner, walking the same route and logging readings each time.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Twelve joints**, two at each hip and one at each knee, move the four legs.
- **Five stereo camera pairs** give 360-degree perception for obstacle avoidance.
- **A 605 Wh battery** powers the robot, with about 90 minutes typical runtime.
- **Payload rails and ports** carry inspection sensors or an arm.
- **Autonomy services** record and replay routes, called missions in the developer docs.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Size (L × W × standing H)** | 1100 × 500 × 840 mm |
| **Net weight** | 32.5 kg |
| **Ingress protection** | IP54 |
| **Operating temperature** | −20 °C to 45 °C |
| **Slopes** | ±30° |
| **Max step height** | 300 mm |
| **Charge time** | 120 minutes |

## Key terms

- **Stereo camera**: two cameras whose views give depth.
- **Mission**: a recorded route with actions the robot can repeat autonomously.
- **Docking**: returning to a charging station on its own.
- **IP54**: protection against dust and splashing water.
- **Mobile robot**: a robot that moves around its environment rather than staying bolted down.

## Getting started

1. **Read the official Spot product page** and list three inspection tasks it targets.
2. **Read "About Spot" in the developer docs** for the full specification tables.
3. **Watch an official Boston Dynamics video** and note where Spot uses stairs.
4. **Compare it with ANYmal and Unitree Go2** on mass, runtime and price.

## Used in

- **Related node:** Boston Dynamics Spot covers the same robot from the SDK and research side.

lessons.name: Stanford Pupper
lessons.summary: Stanford Pupper is a small, open-source Raspberry Pi quadruped from the Stanford Student Robotics club that can trot, hop and run for hands-on teaching.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Stanford Pupper is a small, open-source Raspberry Pi quadruped from the Stanford Student Robotics club that can trot, hop and run for hands-on teaching.

![Photo of the Stanford Pupper quadruped](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-pupper.webp)
*Photo of the Stanford Pupper quadruped. Source: [Stanford Student Robotics; photo credit Max Morse](https://github.com/stanfordroboticsclub/StanfordQuadruped), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is built for students:** the docs say its low cost and simple design target enthusiasts from K-12 and beyond.
- **It is meant to be hacked:** new gaits or behaviours like following you are suggested extensions.
- **There is a full course:** the Pupper course covers PID control, kinematics, reinforcement learning and simulation labs.

> **Key idea:** Pupper is a teaching platform, so its docs and labs matter as much as the hardware.

A software analogy: the control loop works like a game loop, reading input, updating state and rendering joint targets.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A Raspberry Pi 4** is the brain in the original documentation.
- **Twelve servo motors**, three per leg, move the feet and body.
- **A PS4 controller** sends commands over Bluetooth, forwarded to the controller over UDP.
- **The controller state machine** picks trot, walk or rest and outputs servo position targets.
- **PyBullet simulation** lets you test motion before using hardware.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Computer (v1)** | Raspberry Pi 4 |
| **Actuators (v1)** | servos, three per leg |
| **Input** | wireless PS4 controller |
| **Parts cost (v1)** | about $900–1000 |
| **Software licence** | MIT |
| **Pupper v3** | Raspberry Pi 5, GIM4305 brushless motors, about $1000 BOM |

> **Watch out:** the original StanfordQuadruped repository is marked end-of-life; check Pupper v3 material before buying parts.

## Key terms

- **Servo**: a motor that holds a commanded angle.
- **State machine**: code that switches between modes such as trot and rest.
- **Inverse kinematics**: computing joint angles from a desired foot position.
- **PID control**: feedback that corrects error using proportional, integral and derivative terms.
- **BOM**: bill of materials, the parts list and cost.

## Getting started

1. **Read the Pupper documentation** home page and controller description.
2. **Clone StanfordQuadruped** and trace `run_robot.py` from input to servo targets.
3. **Do the course PID and kinematics labs** in order.
4. **Simulate a gait in PyBullet** before running hardware.

## Used in

- **Map projects:** Transfer a conservative gait to Bittle, and Prototype a passive leg linkage.
- **Knowledge links:** Gaits & gait cycles, and Leg design & proprioceptive actuation.

lessons.name: Unitree Go2
lessons.summary: Unitree Go2 is a roughly 15 kg consumer and research quadruped from Unitree Robotics with 4D LiDAR, an SDK, and a starting price of $1,600.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Unitree Go2 is a roughly 15 kg consumer and research quadruped from Unitree Robotics with 4D LiDAR, an SDK, and a starting price of $1,600.

![Photo of a Unitree Go2 used by Salvamont, side view](/img/lessons/robots_quadruped-go2.webp)
*Photo of a Unitree Go2 used by Salvamont, side view. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Unitree_Go2_of_Salvamont_side_view.jpg), CC BY 3.0.*

## Why it matters for us

- **It is an affordable reference robot:** the official page lists prices from $1,600 across AIR, PRO, X and EDU versions.
- **It is common in research:** the map links Go2 to five locomotion and safety topics.
- **It exposed LLM risks:** the **RoboPAIR** study jailbroke a deployed Go2's GPT-3.5 interface, often with 100% attack success.

> **Key idea:** Go2 brings research-grade legged hardware to student budgets, but AI-controlled robots need real safety guardrails.

A software analogy: a jailbroken robot is like a prompt-injected web app, except the exploited output is physical motion.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A 4D LiDAR L2** scans 360° × 96° to detect obstacles from 0.05 m.
- **Twelve motors** drive the legs, with peak joint torque about 45 Nm.
- **Unitree's unitree_sdk2** is an official C++ SDK, built with CMake and released under BSD-3-Clause.
- **Software features** include mapping, autonomous path planning, OTA updates and simulation-trained AI gaits.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Mass** | approx. 15 kg |
| **Standing size** | 70 × 31 × 40 cm |
| **Max speed** | approx. 5 m/s (lab test) |
| **Peak joint torque** | approx. 45 Nm |
| **Battery life** | 1–2 h (2–4 h with the EDU long-endurance pack) |
| **Connectivity** | Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, 4G |
| **Price** | from $1,600 |

> **Watch out:** RoboPAIR shows that an LLM filter alone does not make a robot safe; add hard limits below the AI layer.

## Key terms

- **LiDAR**: a laser sensor measuring distance in many directions.
- **SDK**: libraries for writing your own robot programs.
- **CMake**: a build tool that generates compile instructions for C++ projects.
- **Jailbreak**: a prompt that makes a language model ignore its safety rules.
- **OTA update**: an over-the-air software update.

## Getting started

1. **Read the official Go2 page** and compare versions before choosing one.
2. **Build the unitree_sdk2 examples** with CMake, following its README.
3. **Read the RoboPAIR site** to understand the safety findings responsibly.
4. **Practise in MuJoCo or another simulator** before commanding real motion.

## Used in

- **Built by Unitree Robotics.**
- **Knowledge links:** Gaits & gait cycles, RL locomotion with sim-to-real, Perceptive rough-terrain locomotion, Agile & parkour locomotion.
- **Safety link:** Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots.
